habitat: Solitary in thornveld and mixed bushveld, in more open habitat than Red-backed Shrike. It still-hunts from a branch, pole or telephone wire.
summary: A fairly common summer visitor. Grey and black above, white below, with a full black mask and a white wing-bar that is conspicuous in flight. Sexes are alike. First-year birds lack the full black mask. It has less white at the tail base than a Red-backed Shrike and no rufous mantle. Newman says it is normally silent. It arrives late October to November and departs early April. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

similar.note: A male Red-backed Shrike has a rufous mantle. Lesser Grey Shrike is larger, has less white at the tail base and shows a white wing-bar in flight.

calls.description: Newman says it is normally silent. Grade A call from Akchi at Alakol lake, Kazakhstan. The filename is XC145242-Kleine Klapekster_20130708_07_roep.mp3. Kleine Klapekster is the Dutch name, and roep marks it as a call. It is a breeding-ground recording.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common summer visitor that arrives late October to November and departs early April, so the months stored are October through April and the status is summer-migrant. First-year plumage is only the missing mask. Newman says the species is normally silent; the attached file is still the highest-ranked openly licensed call. Population figures and the Kemp code NB were left unchanged.
